ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing quarterly screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the Canadian sanctions list pursuant to the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (iii) the OFAC SDN and primary sanctions lists (mandatory because UberEats and DoorDash payout in USD require U.S. clearing banks); (iv) FINTRAC-covered politically exposed persons (PEPs) of domestic and foreign jurisdictions per FINTRAC guidance; and (v) publicly available adverse-media legal and regulatory enforcement lists. Screening results must be documented in the corporate AML/KYC file and refreshed before each new payment rail onboarding and annually thereafter; any PEP match triggers heightened source-of-funds verification and Senior Management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via https://www.albertaca.com and authorized corporate registry service providers using the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be submitted in English or French, the working languages of the Alberta registry; a name in any other language or using non-Latin script must be accompanied by an official English or French translation and a Roman-script transliteration, and the NUANS search and registry records will reflect the translated/transliterated form. The name must not be misleading on transliteration, especially in relation to the food delivery and hospitality sector.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal, Crown, Government, Official, Municipal, Police
Canada, Alberta, Calgary, Edmonton or any geographic term suggesting governmental sponsorship without ministerial consent
Cooperative, Credit Union (reserved to licensed cooperatives)
Lawyer, Legal, Barristers (reserved to regulated legal professionals)
Doctor, Medical, Pharmaceutical, Pharmacy (subject to provincial licensing consent)
Public, Non-Profit, Foundation (subject to exemption or licensing proof)
Obscene words, words that scandalize the public, or words contrary to public policy
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended or renewed for one further 90-day period by filing a renewal request and paying the prescribed renewal fee before expiry. If the Alberta Corporate Registry rejects the proposed name: (1) the applicant or its authorized agent may submit written representations within 30 days of the rejection notice requesting reconsideration, including evidence of third-party consent where the rejection is based on a sensitive or regulated token; (2) the applicant may amend the name and file a fresh NUANS search; and (3) if reconsideration fails, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under section 12 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) for an order directing the Registrar to accept the name. Legal counsel should draft the appeal submissions to establish distinctiveness, corporate-object fitness, and non-confusion under the common-law passing-off standard.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable: a licensed third-party registered agent may supply the statutory registered office in Alberta, provided it is a physical municipal street address within Alberta attended during normal business hours for service of process and notices; a P.O. Box, mailbox kiosk, or out-of-province address is invalid under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). The operational ghost kitchen itself must be separately registered at a municipally licensed commercial kitchen facility in Alberta and may not use the registered office as its trading address for Alberta Health Services (AHS) licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5% annual likelihood of an unannounced corporate-registry verification visit or correspondence-based audit of the registered office by Service Alberta; in contrast, the operating kitchen site is subject to a mandatory 100% pre-opening AHS health inspection and thereafter routine unannounced inspections with approximately 25-50% annual recurrence, requiring exact matching of operational site records, municipal business licensing, and insurance certificates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 9-11 (incorporation), ss 104-110 (directors and officers), and s 207 (registered office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta; electronic filing through the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registrar; Certificate of Incorporation issued upon approval
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). The corporation may incorporate with one class of common shares having no par value and nominal consideration. Funds received for unissued shares are held in trust by the corporation; shares may be issued for money, property, or past services at fair value as resolved by the board. Escrow accounts are not required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation accepts the incorporator's subscription for 100,000 common shares at $0.01 per share, and upon receipt of the aggregate subscription amount, the directors are authorized to allot, issue and deliver those shares as fully paid and non-assessable. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the Alberta address stated in the Notice of Registered Office filed with the Articles of Incorporation, and that the Secretary take all steps to maintain that registration. RESOLVED that the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until successors are appointed. DATED as of the date of execution by the undersigned directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (NUANS search through a registered service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search report to verify that the proposed business name is distinguishable from existing corporate, trademark, and legal entity names. If the proposed name is clear, reserve the corporate name or alternatively select a numbered corporation name such as '1234567 Alberta Ltd.' for ghost kitchen and virtual brand operations.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in English or French
Certified trademark search results if brand name is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report identifies a conflict, obtain a revised name and submit a supplemental NUANS report. Re-file the articles under a corrected name; no substantive cure is available for name refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed electronic format. Include the authorised share structure, restrictions on business, first registered office address, and first directors. Prepare the Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, and any other statutory filing forms required for an Alberta business corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry issues a correction query, amend the defective filing within 10 business days through the my?id Alberta online account. Resubmission without duplicate fees is permitted if no certificate has been issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Online Portal (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Alberta Corporate Registry portal, upload the prepared Articles and statutory notices, and pay the applicable incorporation fee by credit card, debit card, or authorised corporate registry service provider account. Retain the transaction reference number and proof of payment in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation in electronic PDF or XML format
Service provider authorisation if using a legal agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment fails or the portal times out, contact the Corporate Registry helpdesk before resubmitting. Do not duplicate the filing until the registry confirms whether a certificate has been issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registrar approves the articles, download the Certificate of Incorporation from the Corporate Registry portal. Verify that the legal name, date of incorporation, registered office, and jurisdiction shown on the certificate are correct before proceeding with board governance and licensing activities.
required_dossiers: Corporate Registry transaction or application ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an administrative error, submit an Application for Correction to the Registrar within 30 days; a statutory correction fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Organizational Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Corporate Minute Book (no government filing required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first directors convene a board meeting to adopt the bylaws, approve the share subscription and issue share certificates, fix the fiscal year end, appoint officers, authorize bank account opening, and approve the corporate seal if used. Record all resolutions in the corporate minute book and register the directors in the register of directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting cannot be held due to lack of quorum, pass a written consent resolution signed by all directors and file it in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Incorporation to obtain a federal Business Number through the CRA business registration portal. Register for the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account if taxable supplies exceed the small supplier threshold, payroll deductions account for employees, and the Alberta corporate tax account. This is essential for ghost kitchen payroll, sales tax compliance, and delivery platform payout reporting.
required_dossiers: First board resolution authorising tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA business number is not issued immediately, confirm the corporate status with the Alberta Corporate Registry and resubmit the application; for persistent issues, call the CRA business enquiries line with the incorporation certificate reference.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Health Services - Environmental Public Health; municipal business licensing authority in the city of operation; Alberta Municipal Affairs - Safety Services for building and fire code compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Operating Permit under the Food Regulation (Alberta Regulation 31/2006) and Municipal Business Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory full EIA reporting for a delivery-only indoor food preparation facility; registration is not required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act unless the facility installs emergency diesel generators, discharges wastewater outside municipal sewer limits, or enters a substance release threshold. A municipal development permit and stormwater/wastewater connection approval are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent must meet municipal sewer standards, e.g., Calgary Sewer Bylaw limits: pH 5.5-11.0, oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L for mineral oil or 150 mg/L for fat/oil/grease, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, and BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L. Install an approved grease interceptor; kitchen exhaust hoods and duct systems must comply with NFPA 96 and ASHRAE 62.1 ventilation standards. Food waste must be handled by a licensed waste carrier and may not be discharged to municipal sewers or storm drains.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Life Safety Certificate of Occupancy from the municipal fire marshal, structural and load-bearing inspection for commercial cooking equipment and exhaust hoods, Alberta Occupational Health and Safety clearance including hazard assessment, emergency response plan, WHMIS program, fire extinguisher inspection, and workplace safety orientation before employee onboarding.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada. Primary registration portal: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html. Ongoing compliance and filed-return access are managed through My Business Account at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services/business-account.html; Alberta provincial corporate tax filings are submitted through the CRA portal for the combined T2/AT1 return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The operator must first incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act RSA 2000 c B-9 (or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act and extra-provincially register in Alberta). The corporation then obtains a nine-digit CRA Business Number (BN) with program accounts in a single BRO application; the GST/HST program account carries the 'RT' prefix, and payroll (RC), corporate income tax (RC), or import/export (RM) accounts can be activated concurrently. Registration is mandatory within 30 days after worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (Excise Tax Act s. 148); a ghost-kitchen enterprise with delivery revenue should register immediately since actual turnover normally exceeds the threshold from the first quarter. CRA identity verification requires the Certificate of Incorporation, Alberta registered office information, director/officer details, and a resident agent if applicable; non-resident ownership is permitted, while Alberta director-residency requirements apply. The BN is issued within 1–5 business days, and the effective registration date can be backdated or prospective as elected on Form RC1.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Alberta business corporation is a separate taxpayer under subsection 2(2)(a) of the Income Tax Act and files a federal T2 return together with the Alberta Corporate Tax and Economic Diversification return. Territorial scope: resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income; a corporation incorporated in Canada is deemed resident under subsection 250(4), so a Canadian parent of a ghost-kitchen brand cannot be treated as a tax-transparent entity. For a foreign-owned non-CCPC, the combined headline corporate rate is federal general 15% plus Alberta general 8% = 23% on active business income (no small-business deduction is available because CCPC status requires Canadian-resident control). For an Alberta-controlled CCPC, the combined small-business rate is federal 9% plus Alberta 8% = 17% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, subject to the Alberta small-business limit. Alberta has no provincial sales tax; only the 5% federal GST applies to taxable supplies in Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification election. Available statutory elections relevant to this structure include: (1) ITA s. 85(1) rollover election (Form T2057) to transfer capital assets, goodwill, or IP into the corporation at agreed tax values; (2) ITA s. 89(4) election to treat a capital dividend account balance as a tax-free capital dividend (Form T2054); (3) ITA s. 93(1)(a) election on foreign affiliate surplus distributions; (4) Excise Tax Act s. 156 election between closely related corporations to deem intercompany taxable supplies to be for nil consideration; (5) Excise Tax Act s. 167 election for the supply of a going concern to be GST-free; (6) ETA s. 191 elections available to financial institutions only, not relevant here; and (7) hybrid-mismatch adjustments under ITA ss. 18.6–18.7, where a taxpayer may elect the manner in which a domestic deduction is reduced or matched with an inclusion in respect of an imported hybrid mismatch arrangement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Alberta applies only the federal 5% GST; no Alberta provincial sales tax or HST surcharge is imposed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. The small-supplier registration threshold under ETA s. 148 is CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding financial services and capital property) measured in the current calendar quarter or in the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters. A ghost-kitchen operator that simultaneously sells through UberEats and DoorDash must aggregate revenue across all sales channels, including marketplace commissions and delivery fees, in applying the threshold. Once exceeded, the corporation must register within 30 days and file from the earlier effective date normally the date on which revenue exceeded the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping regime, and no government-side invoice validation. The CRA operates a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing initiative based on the PEPPOL network (pilot launched 2023; GSF 1.0 profile); participation is optional. A GST registrant must issue tax invoices satisfying ETA s. 169(2): supplier name and BN/RT account, recipient name, invoice date, description, taxable amount, and GST amount at each rate; electronic invoices in PDF/XML are accepted without prior CRA authorization. For marketplace sales, the platform is not a settlement authority for tax, but CRA's marketplace operator rules (ETA s. 233.01, effective 1 July 2021) deem certain platform operators to be the supplier of goods in relation to non-resident vendors. For a domestic Alberta ghost kitchen selling through UberEats and DoorDash, the operator remains the supplier of the prepared food and must collect 5% GST on the full selling price, while the platform's commission or delivery fee is a separate taxable supply to the operator. GST returns are filed electronically; reporting frequency is monthly where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 6,000,000, quarterly where annual supplies exceed CAD 500,000, and annual otherwise. Net tax is remitted via CRA My Payment; input tax credits and any zero-rating refunds are claimed on the same return.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.prepared_food_taxability_context: Supplies of prepared food and warm beverages are taxable at 5% GST; basic groceries (raw, unserved staples) are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part III of the Excise Tax Act. A ghost kitchen that sells cooked meal kits, hot-cooked entrees, salads, or cut fruit through delivery platforms is generally making taxable supplies of prepared food at 5%. Delivery charges invoiced to the consumer as part of the food sale follow the rate of the underlying food; zero-rated groceries with delivery remain zero-rated only where the underlying item is a basic grocery. Commission charges from delivery platforms are taxable services subject to 5% GST and are creditable as input tax credits to the operator.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.cross_border_and_platform_note: Although the payment rails are UberEats and DoorDash payouts, the GST nexus for the ghost kitchen is Canadian domestic supply. Neither platform operates as a 'marketplace operator' that displaces the domestic restaurant for GST purposes; the CRA administrative position requires the restaurant to register, charge, and remit GST on the food supply. The platform may, however, be treated as an agent collecting consideration on behalf of the restaurant; the operator must retain payout statements, commission invoices, and settlement reports for audit trail completeness.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act to (a) goods supplied to a non-resident for export, where the supplier exports the goods or delivers them to a common carrier for direct export (s. 5); (b) services supplied to a non-resident, unless the service relates to real property in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance (s. 7); and (c) intangible personal property such as royalties, trademarks, or licensing rights supplied to a non-resident (s. 10). For this ghost-kitchen/virtual-brand model, prepared-food sales delivered to Canadian consumers are never zero-rated merely because the delivery platform is US-owned. Export zero-rating may be available only for genuine flows, for example: a US master-franchisee paying royalty/licensing fees for the virtual brand, recipes, and management software (zero-rated under s. 10); or food produced in Canada and exported to a US buyer where title and possession pass outside Canada. Services performed partly in Canada for a non-resident that is not registered for GST can be zero-rated where the supply is not connected to Canadian real property or Canadian tangible property, and the operator obtains written proof of the non-resident status and the foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), or digital proof of export where a mandatory declaration applies to the food category
Commercial invoice with export certification terms (Incoterms, FOB/CIF values, CAD equivalent, consignee identification)
Through Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or over-the-road waybill evidencing movement out of Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank FX settlement statement confirming receipt of USD/CAD export proceeds into the Canadian corporate bank account
US customs entry documentation (CBP Form 7501) or ISF 10+2 filing where exports cross via US land border
CRA Form GST171C 'Proof of Export' or an equivalent CRA-accepted third-party certificate (customs broker statement, port authority certificate, independent carrier attestation)
Proof of delivery dated within 60 days of the original supply confirming export completion
CUSMA certificate of origin and any CFIA export permit applicable to food products destined for foreign markets
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA treats zero-rated export claims as high-risk, especially for food products and IP royalties. If documentation is not retained for the statutory period (two years for proof of export and six years for books and records), the CRA reverses the zero-rating, reassesses GST at 5%, disallows associated input tax credits, and charges prescribed interest compounded daily from the original due date. Civil penalties include: a 50% gross-negligence penalty under ETA s. 285; a 25% repeated-failure penalty under ETA s. 293; and false-statement offenses under ETA s. 327(1) with fines up to CAD 25,000 and/or 12 months imprisonment on summary conviction, with higher indictable penalties for deliberate tax evasion. Income Tax Act exposure also applies under s. 239 for fraudulent export claims. On the FX repatriation side, failure to bring export proceeds back to Canada within 180 days can create an 'overdue amount' under amended ITA s. 17(1), triggering deemed interest income at prescribed rates; if the receivable is owed by a non-resident shareholder or a related party, the 180-day outstanding balance may also be recharacterized as a shareholder loan or benefit under ITA s. 15(2) and exposed to 25% Part XIII withholding tax or Part I taxable-benefit clawbacks. The operator should align export invoicing, freight documents, customs entries, and FX receipts in a single auditable file to withstand CRA international and GST audit programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority; bank prudential supervision is administered by OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions); FINTRAC administers Canadian AML/CFT transaction reporting; Statistics Canada collects cross-border direct investment data. Canada abolished general exchange controls in 1951 and no government body retains discretionary FX approval powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible. Both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted; there is no inward or outward remittance approval regime, no conversion quota, and no repatriation licensing requirement. The only friction for profit remittance is the non-resident withholding tax on dividends under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced depending on residency), which is a tax compliance mechanism rather than an FX control. Capital accounts are fully open for non-resident direct investment, subject to Investment Canada Act net benefit review for large acquisitions and the national security review regime. For a small ghost kitchen operating corporation, dividend and shareholder-loan repayments to a non-resident parent are permitted without Bank of Canada approval, provided the solvency tests under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and the withholding tax obligations are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender ratio, no holding period, and no mandatory conversion timeline for export proceeds or foreign currency receipts, including marketplace payouts from UberEats and DoorDash. A Canadian operator may maintain foreign currency accounts at any Schedule I chartered bank and retain USD proceeds indefinitely. The operative compliance requirements are: (i) FINTRAC record-keeping and reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) for electronic funds transfers of C$10,000 or more, including wire originator and beneficiary records; (ii) Statistics Canada reporting for capital transactions; and (iii) CRA functional currency reporting if the corporation elects a US-dollar functional currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD) plus USD Concentration Account; Capital Escrow Account for share subscription proceeds
Operating Account (CAD) and dedicated payment-receivable account for third-party marketplace settlements (UberEats, DoorDash)
Capital Escrow Account plus Payroll Operating Account
USD Operating Account for cross-border vendor disbursements and Letter of Credit issuance
CAD Operating and Payroll Account with Alberta-focused relationship management

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH, but only as a secondary collection rail for delivery-platform payouts; never as the primary treasury account. Legal constraints: (a) foreign EMIs are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in Canada and cannot accept deposits; they operate as registration-only money service businesses through a partner Schedule I bank; (b) funds held with an EMI are not CDIC-insured; (c) under the Retail Payment Activities Act, any payment service provider serving Canadian users must be registered with the Bank of Canada, so the EMI's registration status must be verified in advance; (d) CRA payroll, source-deduction, and GST/HST remittances should be funded from a Schedule I bank account to preserve the prescribed financial institution audit trail and CRA payment integrity; (e) EMI multi-currency rails (e.g., Wise Platform, Airwallex, Payoneer) are viable for receiving USD-denominated UberEats/DoorDash payouts and for low-value international supplier payments, but the treasury policy must require a daily zero-balance sweeper into the primary Schedule I operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for an Alberta business corporation. No physical branch appearance is statutorily required under OSFI Guideline B-8 (AML/CFT Deterrence) or FINTRAC identity-verification rules; identity may be verified through a bank's digital identity scan, Alberta Corporate Registry lookup, and a live video interview with the relationship manager. In practice, all five Tier 1 banks require: (i) a corporate resolution and authorized signing-officer certificate; (ii) certified copies of the federal or Alberta incorporation certificate and annual return (Corporate Access Number); (iii) a beneficial ownership schedule identifying every individual with 25% or more ownership; (iv) video KYC of the director and signing officers using passport-plus-tax-ID documents; (v) a 12-month cash flow projection and business plan for the ghost kitchen; (vi) for non-resident UBOs, a notarized passport and tax-residence certificate. The video interview is mandatory when any non-Canadian beneficial owner exists; in-person attendance is only required if enhanced due diligence cannot electronically verify identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blocker: multi-brand delivery structure - multiple virtual brands (UberEats menu names) settling into one corporate account is flagged under FINTRAC EDD indicators as a possible nominee or layering arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete brand-to-entity ownership map; federal trademark registrations from CIPO for each virtual brand; platform merchant agreements with UberEats, DoorDash, and SkipTheDishes; monthly platform settlement CSV exports mapped to the single operating account; and a board-approved organizational chart demonstrating that the brands are unincorporated product lines of the same legal entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blocker: non-resident shareholder injection - inbound wire from Hong Kong or mainland China for share capital with ambiguous purpose code.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing the exempt share issue; signed subscription agreement; source-of-funds evidence from the remitting shareholder (3 to 6 months of bank statements and net-worth certificate); tax-residence certificate of the shareholder; China-Canada Tax Treaty (1986) analysis confirming treaty eligibility; Investment Canada Act non-reviewable status memo; and Statistics Canada FDI-C reporting form prepared for the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blocker: high USD turnover with no corresponding CAD operating history - the account may appear to be a shell warehouse for marketplace proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical revenue build-up: 12 months of DoorDash and UberEats settlement statements; CPA-reviewed or audited financial statements; kitchen lease and utility invoices; Alberta hotel (food-safety) permit and insurance certificates; IT and ERP logs linking order IDs to payment rails; and a treasury memo explaining the USD/CAD revenue mix together with the FX hedging policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blocker: sudden high-value supplier disbursements to third parties in unrelated geographies - a common feature of ghost kitchen franchise and procurement models.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade-payables ledger; signed supplier purchase orders and matching invoices; counterparty UBO identification and jurisdiction documentation; correspondent-bank relationship confirmation; and, where letters of credit are used, the SWIFT MT700 field 77B sender-to-applicant narrative attached to the underlying commercial contract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for a non-resident shareholder funding the Alberta entity: (1) Wire via SWIFT MT103 with field 50K containing the full legal originator name and address, and field 59 containing the full beneficiary account at the Schedule I bank; (2) use a BPM6-aligned payment purpose code reflecting direct investment - equity capital injection; include in field 70 the narrative 'Share subscription and capital contribution, not a loan, agreement dated [date]'; (3) pre-deliver to the receiving bank's global transaction banking desk a board resolution, the subscription agreement, and the bank's inward remittance disclosure form so that compliance can pre-clear the purpose code; (4) if the inbound transaction exceeds C$1,000,000, file Statistics Canada's Report of Foreign Direct Investment in Canada (form FDI-C) within 20 business days after month-end; (5) no exchange control authorization is required in Canada, but an inbound wire from the United States will be screened against OFAC and corporate transparency records by the US remitting bank; (6) the CAD proceeds must remain in the Capital Escrow Account until the share certificate is issued and the Alberta corporate securities register is updated under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade and operating settlements: (A) Canadian domestic CAD payables (vendors, payroll, CRA) - use Payments Canada Lynx same-day wire or pre-authorized debit under CPA Rule A4; these are domestic rails, not cross-border. (B) US and international supplier payments up to USD 100,000 - use SWIFT MT103 with the intermediary bank identified in field 56A, or Canada-US ACH (via the Clearing House) for amounts below USD 50,000; the remittance narrative must carry the commercial invoice reference and the ISO country code of the beneficiary. (C) Larger procurement - kitting, leasehold equipment, and food-technology software from US vendors - use a documentary letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 (ICC UCP 600) with the Alberta entity as applicant; for recurring vendor financing, a standby LC (MT760) under ISP98 or URDG 758. (D) Delivery-platform payouts from UberEats and DoorDash arrive as USD or CAD ACH or wire from the platform's US treasury; the company must maintain a settlement-ready account with a dedicated ABA routing number and, for USD receipts, a segregated USD ledger so the bank's FX desk can net the conversion. (E) All outbound payment instructions must be FINTRAC-compliant, including full originator fields in SWIFT MT103 field 50K, to avoid rejection by US correspondent banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (spot to 12-month vanilla tenors) executed with the relationship bank under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's standard FX confirmation; must be supported by a board-approved treasury and hedging policy that documents the ghost kitchen's net USD receivable exposure.

FX swaps (same-currency CAD/USD maturity swaps, up to 12 months) used strictly to realign settlement cash-flow mismatches between USD platform payouts and CAD operating disbursements; speculative use is prohibited by internal policy.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) permissible where the company carries USD-denominated equipment leases or franchise financing requiring conversion to CAD; to be executed only with an OSFI-regulated counterparty and designated under IFRS 9 hedge accounting, or fair-valued under ASPE 3856 for private entities.

European-style FX options (CAD puts versus USD calls) permissible to protect the projected USD revenue stream against CAD appreciation; option premiums expensed as operating cost and the hedges documented under the FX policy.

CME-listed CAD/USD futures (contract code R6) permitted for short-dated tenors through a CIRO-registered futures broker, subject to daily variation margin; positions must be reconciled daily against the open forecast receivable ledger.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted and are not relevant because CAD is fully convertible and freely deliverable onshore; any NDF proposal on CAD would be rejected by the bank's derivatives desk and would breach the company's deliverable-only hedging policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months following the incorporation anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty CAD 100 per filing; continued non-compliance may result in a Notice of Intent to Dissolve and administrative strike-off under ABCA s. 216(1), extinguishing corporate powers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset size threshold under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Every corporation must appoint an auditor unless the corporation is non-distributing and all shareholders unanimously consent in writing to dispense with that appointment for the fiscal year. Any shareholder may trigger an audit requirement by written demand.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS required for distributing corporations; private corporations may elect IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook, Part II.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: ABCA does not impose a separate annual UBO filing with Alberta Corporate Registry. Share transfer transactions must be recorded in the Register of Members and a Register of Transfers. Where the significant control (ISC) regime applies, the corporation must maintain an ISC register, verify its accuracy annually, and update the register within 15 days of any change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (Federal 15% + Alberta 8% general corporate rate; reduced to 11% for Canadian-controlled private corporations on first CAD 500,000 active business income: Federal 9% + Alberta 2%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) for CCPCs on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; 10% investment tax credit for qualified property; accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) for clean energy equipment; scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via CRA's e-file (NETFILE) or approved third-party software; paper filing available for certain entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., if year-end is December 31, deadline is June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross sales, service revenue, and other income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source revenue; non-resident corporations must file T2 if they carry on business in Canada or dispose of taxable Canadian property.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions (cost of goods sold, operating expenses, capital cost allowance, etc.)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses reasonably incurred to earn Canadian-source income; allocate expenses per Part IV rules for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (revenue minus deductions, adjusted for loss carryovers)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply non-capital loss carryforwards (20 years) and capital loss carryforwards (3 years back, indefinite forward) as per Part I rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable (15% of taxable income, reduced by SBD and credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are subject to Part I tax on Canadian-source business income; treaty relief may reduce rate if permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax payable (Alberta 8% general, 2% for SBD-eligible income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Alberta corporate tax applies to income allocated to Alberta; non-residents with a permanent establishment in Alberta must file provincial return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeated failure penalty up to 10% of unpaid tax; interest on late payments at prescribed rate (currently 8% for 2025).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid to non-residents (Part XIII tax); reduced to 15% under Canada-US Tax Treaty (5% if shareholder owns at least 10% of voting shares).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US) to the Canadian payer before payment. Payer must complete Form NR301 (Application for Treaty-Based Waiver) and submit to CRA. Alternatively, file Form NR7 to request a refund of excess withholding within two years of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%; treaty rate 10% (Canada-US) for copyrights, patents, trademarks, etc. Interest: statutory 25%; treaty rate 15% (Canada-US) for arm's length interest; 0% for certain arm's length long-term debt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50 million in gross revenue or CAD 250 million in total assets (for the group) triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation under CRA's TP documentation requirements; smaller entities should maintain contemporaneous documentation to avoid penalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like UAE, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions (e.g., OECD BEPS Action 6) require substantive business presence and economic activity to claim treaty benefits. A ghost kitchen with only a mailbox and no operational staff in Canada may be deemed a shell company and denied treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting revenue from delivery platforms (UberEats, DoorDash) or claiming fictitious expenses to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239: fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties of 50% of tax evaded plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under s.227.1 if they failed to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset freezes possible under CRA's collection powers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating in Canada solely to access treaty benefits or tax incentives without real business operations (e.g., no employees, no physical kitchen, no management in Canada).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under GAAR; reassessment of tax with penalties up to 25% of tax avoided; potential criminal charges for fraudulent misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in the sham; CRA can pierce corporate veil to recover taxes from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as a money services business (MSB) if handling large cash transactions or cross-border transfers; not implementing AML compliance program for delivery payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: fines up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal liability for directors and officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to CAD 500,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years for knowingly failing to comply with AML obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length prices to related foreign entities (e.g., royalty payments to a parent in a low-tax jurisdiction) without proper documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust prices and impose penalties under s.247(3): 10% of the net adjustment (if gross negligence) plus interest; double taxation risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they signed false or misleading TP documentation; criminal liability for tax evasion if intentional.
